tools.name: verify-email
tools.title: Verify Email
tools.description: Verify whether a single email address is deliverable using Bouncer. Returns a verdict of deliverable, risky, undeliverable, or unknown, a score out of 100, a send or suppress recommendation, and the domain and account signals behind it. Spends one Bouncer credit per address.

tools.name: verify-domain
tools.title: Verify Domain
tools.description: Check a domain's mail setup with Bouncer. Returns whether it publishes a working MX record, whether it is a catch-all, disposable, free, or toxic domain, and which mail provider it uses. Use this when asked about a domain rather than a specific mailbox. Spends one Bouncer credit.

tools.name: get-credits
tools.title: Get Bouncer Credits
tools.description: Get the number of Bouncer verification credits remaining on the account. Does not spend a credit.

ai.instructions:
- Each verify-email or verify-domain call spends one Bouncer credit. Verify only the addresses the user actually asked about, and never re-verify an address you already have a result for in this conversation.
- Report the verdict and the recommendation together. A verdict of deliverable alone does not mean an address is worth sending to.
- The roleAddress and freeProvider signals are Bouncer heuristics over the local part and the domain. They misfire on personal addresses such as mail@ or contact@, so report them as information and never as a defect.
- A signal value of "Unknown" means Bouncer could not determine it. Never report it as "No".
- When didYouMean is returned, surface the suggested correction and offer to verify it instead.
- If a call fails because the account is out of credits, say so plainly and stop; do not retry.

evals.input: @bouncer-email-verifier does example.com have a working mail server?
@bouncer-email-verifier how many verification credits do I have left?
